items.place: Jully Central Jail, Itanagar · Geku, Upper Siang, Arunachal Pradesh
items.headline: Four Siang dam protesters freed after 29 days
items.text: Four Geku villagers held under Arunachal's anti-terror law since 9 October were freed as a state "goodwill gesture" before talks. Six others remain detained; the state says FIR withdrawals must follow legal process.

photo.alt: A wide river with sandbanks and a long bridge, seen between forested hills, under a cloudy sky.
photo.caption: The Siang river near Pasighat, downstream of Upper Siang where the four villagers live, in 2023.

items.headline: Kaziranga activist Pranab Doley walks free
items.text: Land-rights activist Pranab Doley left Golaghat jail on Friday evening after the High Court quashed his NSA detention. He called the NSA's use arbitrary; no Assam government response was reported.

photo.alt: Tall grass in the foreground and a lone tree on flat grassland under a blue sky.
photo.caption: Grassland in Kaziranga National Park, Assam, near the hotel site Doley protested against, in 2023.

items.place: Gali Sheesh Mahal, Chawri Bazar, Old Delhi
items.headline: Six workers die in Old Delhi building collapse
items.text: Six workers from Bihar died when an unauthorised building under construction collapsed in Chawri Bazar. Police arrested the owner on Saturday and three contractors on Friday on culpable homicide charges.

photo.alt: A crowded market street lined with old buildings and tangled wires, with cycle rickshaws and porters, and a red-stone mosque dome at the far end.
photo.caption: Chawri Bazar road in Old Delhi, with the Jama Masjid at the end, in 2005.

items.headline: Assam says police expelled 28 alleged Bangladeshis
items.text: Assam's chief minister said Sribhumi police detected and expelled 28 people they describe as Bangladeshis living illegally. The report names no court or tribunal process; no Bangladeshi response was reported.

photo.alt: A wet main road with a cycle rickshaw, auto-rickshaw, roadside stalls and billboards under a grey sky.
photo.caption: Karimganj–Silchar Road near Karimganj bus station, in the district now called Sribhumi, in 2019.

items.headline: Strikes on village near Sanaa kill 27
items.text: Strikes on al-Shariya village north of Sanaa killed at least 27 people, mostly women and children, Houthi health officials said, blaming the Saudi-led coalition. Saudi Arabia and Yemen's government have not commented.

photo.alt: A narrow lane between tall brick tower houses with decorated windows, a parked motorbike and a water tank.
photo.caption: A lane in Sanaa's old city in 2013. Saturday's strikes hit al-Shariya village, north of the capital.

items.place: Deir el-Balah, Gaza City and Khan Younis, Gaza
items.headline: First winter storm floods Gaza's tent camps
items.text: The season's first storm flooded about 70,000 tents of displaced families, Gaza's media office said; aid groups blame Israeli limits on shelter materials. No Israeli response was reported.

photo.alt: People in dark clothing stand among plastic-sheet tents in heavy rain on muddy ground.
photo.caption: Flooded tents of displaced Palestinians after heavy rain in Deir el-Balah, Gaza, in 2025.
photo.credit: Ashraf Amra / UNRWA, via Wikimedia Commons

items.place: Paris, Lyon and cities across France
items.headline: Cost-of-living protests sweep France again
items.text: About 146,000 people protested across France, the interior ministry said; unions said 250,000. Police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon and say 200 people attacked officers during an arrest.

photo.alt: A bronze statue of a woman holding an olive branch on a tall stone monument, against a blue sky.
photo.caption: The Monument to the Republic at Place de la République, Paris, a usual rally point, in 2026.

items.headline: Fear grows in Damazin as fighting spreads
items.text: Damazin residents reported power, water and grain-mill cuts and families fleeing as fighting spread in Blue Nile; one resident said the city was calm. No army or RSF statement was reported.

photo.alt: Rooftops and a tall beige building seen through the branches of a leafy tree under a hazy sky.
photo.caption: A street view in Damazin, capital of Blue Nile, in 2019.

items.place: La Restinga, El Hierro, Canary Islands, Spain
items.headline: Canary island declares emergency over boat arrivals
items.text: El Hierro declared an emergency and asked Madrid for help after more than 3,300 people arrived on about 30 boats since 1 November. No central government reply was reported.

photo.alt: A small harbour with a dark pebble beach, black lava rocks, sailing masts and a breakwater under a bright sky.
photo.caption: The fishing harbour at La Restinga, El Hierro, where most boats land, in 2005.
photo.credit: Mª. C. Mingorance Rodríguez / Wikimedia Commons

focus.title: The fight over the Siang dam
focus.dek: Four villagers held since 9 October were freed on 7 November as a state "goodwill gesture"; six others remain detained.
focus.alt: A wide, calm river between forested hills, with tall grass in the foreground.

cases.name: Umar Khalid
cases.status: Moved Supreme Court for bail (reported 5 Nov) against Delhi HC's 30 Sep refusal, its third; trial not begun. Delhi Police have called his fresh bail pleas premature under the Supreme Court's one-year bar

cases.name: Sharjeel Imam
cases.status: Moved Supreme Court for bail (reported 5 Nov) against Delhi HC's 30 Sep refusal, saying no prosecution witness has yet been examined. No official response to the new plea reported

cases.name: Srishti Gupta
cases.status: Still jailed; no bail in 2 of 11 cases. A bail order notes she was not at the site of the violence; a police chargesheet calls her a key conspirator. No new developments reported this week

cases.name: Satyam Verma
cases.law: NSA (order 12 May 2026) plus Noida protest FIRs
cases.status: Journalist still held under NSA despite bail in one case on 15 Sep. Allahabad HC reserved its verdict on his NSA challenge on 8 Oct; no judgment reported by 8 Nov. UP Police allege a major role in protest violence

cases.name: Dawit Isaak
cases.status: Journalist held incommunicado 25 years; whereabouts and health unknown. Eritrea's president said in 2009 there would be no trial and no release

cases.name: Abdulhadi Al-Khawaja
cases.status: Human rights defender serving life in Jau Prison; 31 rights groups urged France's president to press for his release during his 19–21 Oct Gulf tour. No Bahraini government response reported

cases.name: Osman Kavala
cases.status: Istanbul court refused release and retrial (reported 14 Oct) despite a binding European Court of Human Rights ruling; government denies the case is political and says courts are independent

cases.name: Jimmy Lai
cases.status: Serving 20 years, aged 78. UK urged his release (22 Oct); Hong Kong rejected this, saying he was not tried for his political views

cases.name: Aung San Suu Kyi
cases.status: Under house arrest in Naypyidaw; her son reported on 22 Oct his first phone call with her in more than five years. Government rejects calls for her release

cases.name: Imran Aliyev
cases.law: Smuggling, money laundering, tax evasion, forgery charges
cases.status: Meclis.info founder; prosecutors sought 12 years (20 Oct); next hearing set for 3 Nov, outcome not yet reported. Authorities say outlets broke foreign-grant rules and deny his torture claims

cases.name: Dr Hussam Abu Safiya
cases.law: Unlawful Combatants Law; no charge, no trial
cases.status: Hospital director held without charge; Supreme Court upheld detention in June and his lawyer reported beatings in July. Israel alleges Hamas links, which family and lawyers deny

cases.name: Detainees held by the RSF
cases.countcap: held in El Geneina, doctors say
cases.status: Amnesty reports torture, forced labour and ransom-for-release in El Fasher; doctors report food shortages and rising deaths in El Geneina. RSF did not respond to Amnesty

cases.name: Najmeh Amini
cases.law: Death sentence for blasphemy; 12.5 years on security charges
cases.status: 23-year-old student held in Mashhad Central (Vakilabad) Prison, sentenced to death over social media posts. No official statement reported
src: Center for Human Rights in Iran

cases.name: Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha
cases.law: Anti-Terrorism Act; earlier 17 years under electronic crimes law (PECA)
cases.status: Human rights lawyers sentenced to 10 years on 29 Oct after trial inside Adiala prison. Law minister says the judiciary is independent

cases.name: Artin Ghazanfari
cases.law: 26 years incl. 'media activities' under espionage-penalties law
cases.status: Baha'i photojournalist with heart failure; judge reportedly refused hospital transfer. Sentence told to him on 26 Oct. Iran did not respond to CPJ

cases.name: Mountaga Tall
cases.status: Lawyer and junta critic abducted in Bamako; his son also vanished on 16 May. Authorities have not acknowledged holding either

cases.name: Zied el-Heni
cases.law: Telecommunications Code art. 86 (1 year); four terrorism-related charges (4 years)
cases.status: Journalist sentenced to four more years on 27 Oct over a leaked-audio report; 17 groups urged his release on 5 Nov. No official response reported
